title: The one who left in anger
hookLine: Yunus gives up on his people, walks off in anger, boards a crowded ship, and is thrown into the sea
carry: walking away is also a choice

cards: Ten explanations. Patience, and more patience. Every approach tried, and still nobody listens.

Then the keys come off the hook, and the door closes, not slammed, just closed hard. A prophet named Yunus has been calling his people to Allah, and they won't have it. The Qur'an says, simply, he went off in anger.
He heads for the sea and boards a ship. Anywhere but here. Then, out at sea, things go wrong.

teach.h: DHU N-NUN: THE ONE OF THE FISH.
teach.b: The Qur'an tells this story in pieces, across several surahs. Surah Al-Anbiya gives him a nickname, in Pickthall's words: “And (mention) Dhu'n-Nun, when he went off in anger.” Dhu n-Nun: the one of the fish.

teach.h: HE FLED UNTO THE LADEN SHIP.
teach.b: Surah As-Saffat has the ship: “When he fled unto the laden ship.” Fled. The Arabic word is the one for a runaway slave leaving his master; that's how the text names what he did.
Commentators explain that Yunus left his people before Allah had given him leave to go. His frustration was understandable. His leaving was still a choice.
Then trouble at sea. The Qur'an doesn't describe it; commentators say the ship was in danger and someone had to go over the side.
They cast lots, and the lot falls on Yunus. He's thrown into the sea, and a great fish swallows him. The Qur'an says he was blameworthy at that moment, and doesn't pretend otherwise.
And yet Yunus is still a prophet, honored by name: the tenth surah is called Yunus.

teach.h: NO ONE IS BETTER THAN YUNUS.
teach.b: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is reported in Sahih al-Bukhari to have said that no one should say he is better than Yunus, son of Matta.

teach.h: WALKING AWAY IS ALSO A CHOICE.
teach.b: Another surah even tells the Prophet: be patient, and don't be like the companion of the fish. The lesson is gentle: Yunus is a warning and a beloved prophet at once, and the one who walked out is not written off.
Jews and Christians know him too, as Jonah, from the Hebrew Bible. For now, leave him where the Qur'an leaves him today: in the dark, inside the fish.

how: Muslims read the story of Yunus in Surahs Yunus, Al-Anbiya, As-Saffat and Al-Qalam, and honor him as a prophet whose story teaches patience with people and turning back to Allah.

o: the man of the sea: a name for sailors
the one of the fish: a name for Yunus
the one of the mountain: a name for shepherds

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.

s: Yunus left his people before Allah gave him leave
commentators explain his leaving this way; the Qur'an says he went off in anger (21:87).
after the fish, the Qur'an stops calling Yunus a prophet
he remains an honored prophet, and a surah bears his name.
the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said no one should claim to be better than Yunus

games.q: Yunus has called his people again and again, and they won't listen. what does he do?
o: keep calling, and wait for Allah's word.
leave them, in anger, on the first ship out.
games.why: he went off in anger (21:87) and fled unto the laden ship (37:140), and the Qur'an calls him blameworthy for it.

practice: Think of a place, a person, a job or a conversation you left in frustration; maybe you were right to be frustrated, and there's no need to argue that.

Just notice the moment of leaving: what it felt like in your body, what you told yourself as you went, whether it was a choice or felt like the only option. If you pray, you can ask Allah to show you what you couldn't see then.

wordCard.voice: Dhu'n-Nun, the one of the fish: Yunus's name for the day he went off in anger and left his people behind.
